risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns calls the accelerated transition to electric mobility one of the key challenges: increasing EV adoption 'is expected to gradually alter demand patterns for conventional internal combustion engine (ICE)-related components, particularly engine and transmission systems, thereby requiring substantial investments in technology upgradation, product diversification, localisation, and research & development.' The Outlook also warns of consolidation and rationalisation across selected conventional product segments.
risks.risk: Electrification of the vehicle parc erodes demand for conventional ICE-related components

risks.note: All products of the Company fall in one primary business segment - Shock Absorber (front forks, rear cushions, struts, gas springs/rear door lifters) - so there is no segmental diversification to absorb a demand shock. The Board's own identified risk list includes 'Over dependence on limited user segment base'.

'Dependence on Collaborators' is one of the risks the Board has explicitly identified. Product and technology access runs through Astemo (Japan) - also an enterprise with significant influence over the Company and the counterparty for royalty, design-and-drawing fees and intangible-asset purchases - while the newer Soben (France) and TFX Suspension (Netherlands) collaborations are 'still at an early stage and have yet to translate into commercial supplies'.

The MD&A flags volatility in raw material prices, inflationary pressures and rising energy and transportation costs; the Board's risk list includes 'Increase in raw material/component prices'. The Chairman states that input-cost volatility, together with the fixed cost of technology and digital-infrastructure investment, 'affected profitability in the short term' in FY 2025-26.
risks.risk: Input-cost volatility and raw-material price increases

risks.note: 'Intensifying Competition' and 'Declining margins' are both named in the Board's identified risk list - a structural pressure for a single-product tier-1 supplier selling to a concentrated OEM customer base.

MD&A cites supply chain disruptions, semiconductor availability, logistics constraints and fluctuations in foreign exchange rates; mitigation is described only as vendor diversification, supply chain monitoring, cost optimisation and liquidity management.
risks.risk: Supply-chain disruption, semiconductor availability and currency exposure

risks.note: MD&A states that stricter emission norms, Bharat NCAP safety regulations and evolving environmental compliance requirements 'may lead to higher capital expenditure and operational costs' for manufacturers and component suppliers. The Board's risk list separately names 'Imposition of strict environmental / safety / regulatory regulations'.
risks.risk: Rising regulatory and compliance cost from emission, safety and environmental norms

risks.note: The Directors' Report discloses that Board strength fell below the six-director minimum under Regulation 17(1)(c) from April 08, 2025 to May 26, 2025 (about 48 days) after Mr. Kazuhiro Nishioka's cessation; a Regulation 30 outcome-of-board-meeting submission to NSE was delayed by about 3 hours 58 minutes; and the Secretarial Auditors observed that certain instances of UPSI sharing were not fully captured in the Structured Digital Database, alongside an observation on timely circulation of draft Minutes.
risks.risk: Listing-compliance and insider-trading control lapses observed during the year
